title.zh: 卷二十 志第一: 天文 日薄食煇珥雲氣 月五星淩犯及星變
title.en: Volume 20 Treatises 1: Astronomy - Solar Eclipses, Lunar and Five Planets Occultations, Changes to Stars
title.raw: 卷二十 志第一: 天文 日薄食煇珥雲氣 月五星淩犯及星變 Volume 20 Treatises 1: Astronomy - Solar Eclipses, Lunar and Five Planets Occultations, Changes to Stars

sentences.zh: 自伏羲仰觀俯察，黃帝迎日推策，重黎序天地，堯曆日月星辰，舜齊七政，周武王訪箕子，陳《洪範》，協五紀，而觀天之道備矣。

translations.literal: From Fuxi, who looked up to observe and looked down to examine, the Yellow Emperor welcomed the sun and pushed the tallies, Chongli ordered Heaven and Earth, Yao calibrated the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, Shun aligned the seven regulators, King Wu of Zhou sought Jizi and set forth the Great Plan, harmonized the five calendars—and thus the Way of observing Heaven was complete.
translations.idiomatic: From Fuxi gazing up and down, the Yellow Emperor taking the sun and reckoning the cycles, Chongli ordering Heaven and Earth, Yao marking sun, moon, and stars, Shun aligning the seven regulators, and King Wu of Zhou questioning Jizi and laying out the Great Plan to harmonize the five calendars—the art of reading Heaven was whole.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，見吉凶，聖人象之。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; fortune and disaster appear; the sage images them."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Heaven hangs forth images; fortune and disaster show themselves; the sage takes them as models."

sentences.zh: 」故孔子因魯史作《春秋》，於日星風雨霜雹雷霆皆書變而不書常，所以明天道、驗人事也。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius, taking the Lu annals, made the Spring and Autumn; for sun, stars, wind, rain, frost, hail, and thunder he recorded change and not the routine, to clarify Heaven's Way and test human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: So Confucius drew on the Lu annals to write the Spring and Autumn: sun, stars, wind, rain, frost, hail, and thunder he logged only when they changed, never the ordinary—to lay bare Heaven's Way and weigh human affairs.

sentences.zh: 秦漢而下，治日患少，陰陽愆違，天象錯迕，無代無之。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, those who governed had little love for it; yin and yang fell out of step, celestial signs clashed and crossed—no age has lacked this.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han, rulers have cared little for such matters; yin and yang slip their measure, and heaven's signs tangle and cross—no dynasty has been free of it.

sentences.zh: 金百有十九年，而日食四十二，星辰風雨霜雹雷霆之變，不知其幾。

translations.literal: Jin endured one hundred nineteen years, yet solar eclipses forty-two; changes among stars, wind, rain, frost, hail, and thunder—who knows how many.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lasted one hundred nineteen years and saw forty-two solar eclipses; stars, wind, rain, frost, hail, and thunder changed beyond count.

sentences.zh: 金九主，莫賢于世宗，二十九年之間，猶日食者十有一，日珥虹貫者四五。

translations.literal: Of Jin's nine rulers, none surpassed Shizong; even in twenty-nine years there were still eleven solar eclipses and four or five of solar halos with rainbows piercing the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Of Jin's nine emperors none matched Shizong—yet even his twenty-nine years brought eleven solar eclipses and four or five halos with rainbows piercing the sun.

sentences.zh: 然終金之世，慶雲環日者三，皆見於世宗之世。

translations.literal: Yet through all Jin, thrice auspicious clouds ringed the sun—all seen in Shizong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yet only thrice in all Jin did auspicious clouds ring the sun—and all three fell in Shizong's reign.

sentences.zh: 羲、和之後，漢有司馬，唐有袁、李，皆世掌天官，故其說詳。

translations.literal: After Xi and He, Han had Sima, Tang had Yuan and Li—all hereditary masters of the celestial offices, so their accounts are full.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi and He, Han had the Sima clan, Tang the Yuan and Li families—each generation held the celestial office, and their lore runs deep.

sentences.zh: 且六合為一，推步之術不見異同。

translations.literal: Moreover the six directions are one realm; the art of calculation shows no variance.
translations.idiomatic: The six directions are one cosmos; the methods of reckoning do not truly diverge.

sentences.zh: 金、宋角立，兩國置曆，法有差殊，而日官之選亦有精粗之異。

translations.literal: Jin and Song stood opposed; each state set its calendar, methods differed, and the choice of officials of the sun likewise ran from fine to coarse.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Song faced each other; each kept its own calendar, the methods differed, and even the astronomers chosen ranged from skilled to crude.

sentences.zh: 今奉詔作《金史》，于志天文，各因其舊，特以《春秋》為准雲。

translations.literal: Now, by imperial decree compiling the History of Jin, in the treatise on astronomy each follows its former records, taking the Spring and Autumn alone as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Now, by decree we compile the History of Jin; in the astronomy treatise we follow each dynasty's own records, but take the Spring and Autumn as the sole standard.

sentences.zh: 日薄食煇珥雲氣

translations.literal: Solar eclipses, halos and spurs, and cloud vapors.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipses, halos and spurs, and cloud vapors.

sentences.zh: 太祖天輔三年夏四月丙子朔，日食。

translations.literal: Taizu, third year of Tianfu, summer, fourth month, first day of the month bingzi: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, third year of Tianfu, summer, fourth month, on bingzi, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 四年冬十月戊辰朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fourth year, winter, tenth month, first day of the month wuchen: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, winter, tenth month, on wuchen, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 六年春二月庚寅朔，日食。

translations.literal: Sixth year, spring, second month, first day of the month gengyin: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, spring, second month, on gengyin, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 七年秋八月辛巳朔，日食。

translations.literal: Seventh year, autumn, eighth month, first day of the month xinsi: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, autumn, eighth month, on xinsi, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太宗天會七年三月己卯，日中有黑子。

translations.literal: Taizong, seventh year of Tianhui, third month, day jimao: black spots within the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, seventh year of Tianhui, third month, on jimao: sunspots in the sun's disk.

sentences.zh: 九月丙午朔，日食。

translations.literal: Ninth month, first day of the month bingwu: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, on bingwu, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月丙午朔，日食。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, first month, first day of the month bingwu: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth year, first month, on bingwu, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天會十四年十一月丙寅，日中有黑子，斜角交行。

translations.literal: Xizong, fourteenth year of Tianhui, eleventh month, day bingyin: black spots within the sun, crossing at a slant.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong, fourteenth year of Tianhui, eleventh month, on bingyin: sunspots in the sun, crossing obliquely.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年七月癸卯朔，日食。

translations.literal: Tianjuan, third year, seventh month, first day of the month guimao: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjuan, third year, seventh month, on guimao, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 皇統三年十二月癸未朔，日食。

translations.literal: Huangtong, third year, twelfth month, first day of the month guiwei: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Huangtong, third year, twelfth month, on guiwei, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 四年六月辛巳朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fourth year, sixth month, first day of the month xinsi: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, sixth month, on xinsi, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五年六月乙亥朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fifth year, sixth month, first day of the month yihai: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, sixth month, on yihai, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 八年四月戊子朔，日食。

translations.literal: Eighth year, fourth month, first day of the month wuzi: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year, fourth month, on wuzi, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 九年三月癸未朔，日食。

translations.literal: Ninth year, third month, first day of the month guiwei: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year, third month, on guiwei, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 海陵庶人天德二年正月甲辰，日有暈珥，白虹貫之。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor Hailing, second year of Tiande, first month, day jiachen: the sun showed a halo and spurs, and a white rainbow pierced it.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor Hailing, second year of Tiande, first month, on jiachen: the sun bore a halo and mock suns, pierced by a white rainbow.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙戌，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day bingxu: a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, on bingxu: a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙卯，慶雲見，狀如鸞鳳，五彩。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day yimao: auspicious clouds appeared, shaped like phoenixes, in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, on yimao: auspicious clouds appeared, shaped like phoenixes in five colors.

sentences.zh: 三年正月丁酉，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, day dingyou: a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, first month, on dingyou: a white rainbow pierced the sun.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年五月癸丑朔，日食。

translations.literal: Zhenyuan, second year, fifth month, first day of the month guichou: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan, second year, fifth month, on guichou, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 三年四月丁丑朔，昏霧四塞，日無光，凡十有七日乃霽。

translations.literal: Third year, fourth month, first day of the month dingchou: dusk haze sealed all four quarters; the sun had no light—for seventeen days in all before it cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, fourth month, on dingchou, the new moon: twilight murk closed in on every side; the sun gave no light for seventeen days before the sky cleared.

sentences.zh: 五月丁未朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day of the month dingwei: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, on dingwei, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 正隆三年三月辛酉朔，有司奏日食，候之不見。

translations.literal: Zhenglong, third year, third month, first day of the month xinyou: the relevant office reported a solar eclipse; on watching, none was seen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglong, third year, third month, on xinyou, the new moon: the calendar office reported an eclipse, but observation found none.

sentences.zh: 海陵敕，自今日食皆面奏，不須頒告中外。

translations.literal: Hailing decreed: from today, every solar eclipse is to be reported to the throne in person—no proclamation to the court within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing decreed that from that day every solar eclipse must be reported to him in person, not announced throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 五年八月丙午朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fifth year, eighth month, first day of the month bingwu: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, eighth month, on bingwu, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 庚午，日中有黑子，狀如人。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: black spots within the sun, shaped like a man.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu: sunspots in the sun shaped like a man.

sentences.zh: 六年二月甲辰朔，日有暈珥，戴背。

translations.literal: Sixth year, second month, first day of the month jiachen: the sun showed a halo and spurs, with an anthelion.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, second month, on jiachen, the new moon: the sun bore a halo and mock suns, with an anthelion behind.

sentences.zh: 十月丙午，慶雲見。

translations.literal: Tenth month, day bingwu: auspicious clouds appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, on bingwu: auspicious clouds appeared.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定二年正月戊辰朔，日食，伐鼓用幣，命壽王京代拜行禮。

translations.literal: Shizong, second year of Dading, first month, first day of the month wuchen: solar eclipse; drums were beaten and silks offered; Prince Shou Jing was ordered to perform the rites in the emperor's stead.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, second year of Dading, first month, on wuchen, the new moon: a solar eclipse; drums were beaten and silks offered, and Prince Shou Jing performed the rites in the emperor's place.

sentences.zh: 為制，凡遇日月虧食，禁酒、樂、屠宰一日。

translations.literal: A regulation was made: whenever sun or moon suffered eclipse or waning, wine, music, and slaughter were forbidden for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He ordained that whenever sun or moon was eclipsed or dimmed, wine, music, and slaughter were forbidden for one day.

sentences.zh: 三年六月庚申朔，日食，上不視朝，命官代拜。

translations.literal: Third year, sixth month, first day of the month gengshen: solar eclipse; the emperor did not hold court and ordered officials to perform the rites in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, sixth month, on gengshen, the new moon: a solar eclipse; the emperor stayed away from court and had officials perform the rites for him.

sentences.zh: 有司不治務，過時乃罷。

translations.literal: The relevant offices did not attend to their duties and only dismissed the matter after the time had passed.
translations.idiomatic: The offices in charge neglected their duties and only stood down long after the hour had passed.

sentences.zh: 後為常。

translations.literal: This afterward became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: That afterward became the rule.

sentences.zh: 四年六月甲寅朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fourth year, sixth month, first day of the month jiayin: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, sixth month, on jiayin, the new moon: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 七年四月戊辰朔，日食，上避正殿、減膳，伐鼓應天門內，百官各于本司庭立，明複乃止。

translations.literal: Seventh year, fourth month, first day of the month wuchen: solar eclipse; the emperor avoided the main hall and reduced his meals; drums were beaten within the Gate of Responding to Heaven; the hundred officials each stood in the courtyard of his own office until brightness returned, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, fourth month, on wuchen, the new moon: a solar eclipse; the emperor left the main hall and cut his meals; drums sounded inside the Gate of Responding to Heaven; every official stood in his own office courtyard until the sun brightened again, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 閏七月己卯午刻，慶雲環日。

translations.literal: Intercalary seventh month, day jimao, at the noon watch: auspicious clouds ringed the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary seventh month, on jimao at the noon watch: auspicious clouds ringed the sun.

sentences.zh: 八月辛亥午刻，慶雲環日。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day xinhai, at the noon watch: auspicious clouds ringed the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, on xinhai at the noon watch: auspicious clouds ringed the sun.

sentences.zh: 九年八月甲申朔，有司奏日當食，以雨不見。

translations.literal: Ninth year, eighth month, first day of the month jiashen: the relevant office reported that the sun ought to be eclipsed, but rain hid it from view.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year, eighth month, on jiashen, the new moon: the calendar office reported an eclipse due, but rain kept it from sight.

sentences.zh: 為近奉安太社，乃伐鼓於社，用幣于應天門內。

translations.literal: Because the Grand Altar of Earth was soon to be installed, drums were beaten at the altar and silks offered within the Gate of Responding to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Grand Altar of Earth was soon to be enshrined, drums were beaten at the altar and silks offered inside the Gate of Responding to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月壬辰朔，日食。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, fifth month, on renchen new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, on renchen new moon in the fifth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十四年十一月甲申朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, eleventh month, on jiashen new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, on jiashen new moon in the eleventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月丙午朔，日食。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, third month, on bingwu new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, on bingwu new moon in the third month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十七年九月丁酉朔，日食。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, ninth month, on dingyou new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, on dingyou new moon in the ninth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十月己未，慶雲見於日側。

translations.literal: Twenty-third year, tenth month, on jiwei: auspicious clouds appeared beside the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, on jiwei in the tenth month, auspicious clouds appeared beside the sun.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬午朔，日食。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renwu new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renwu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 二十八年八月甲子朔，日食。

translations.literal: Twenty-eighth year, eighth month, on jiazi new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, on jiazi new moon in the eighth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 二十九年正月乙卯巳初，日有暈，左右有珥，上有背氣兩重，其色青赤而厚。

translations.literal: Twenty-ninth year, first month, on yimao at the start of si hour: the sun had a halo; left and right had parhelia; above were two layers of counter-glow, their color blue-red and thick.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, on yimao in the first month at the start of si hour, the sun showed a halo with parhelia to left and right and two thick blue-red counter-glows above.

sentences.zh: 複有白虹貫之亙天，其東有戰氣長四尺餘，五刻而散。

translations.literal: Again a white rainbow pierced it spanning heaven; to its east was battle vapor more than four chi long; at the fifth watch it dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: A white rainbow then pierced the sun across the sky; east of it battle vapor stretched over four chi and dispersed at the fifth watch.

sentences.zh: 丁巳巳初，日有兩珥，上有背氣兩重，其色青赤而淡。

translations.literal: On dingsi at the start of si hour: the sun had two parhelia; above were two layers of counter-glow, their color blue-red and pale.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi at the start of si hour the sun had two parhelia and two pale blue-red counter-glows above.

sentences.zh: 頃之，背氣於日上為冠，已而俱散。

translations.literal: Shortly the counter-glow above the sun formed a crown; then all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the counter-glow above the sun formed a crown, then all faded.

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉朔，日食。

translations.literal: Second month, on xinyou new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinyou new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 甲子辰刻，日上有重暈兩*，抱而複背，背而複抱，凡二三次。

translations.literal: On jiazi at the chen watch: on the sun were two layered halos [*]; embracing then again counter-glow, counter-glow then again embracing—altogether two or three times.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi at the chen watch the sun bore two layered halos; embracing vapor and counter-glow alternated two or three times.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，日暈兩珥，有負氣承氣，而白虹亙天，左右有戟氣。

translations.literal: On yichou: the sun had a halo with two parhelia, negative and supporting vapors, and a white rainbow spanning heaven; left and right had halberd vapor.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the sun showed a halo with two parhelia, negative and supporting vapors, a white rainbow across the sky, and halberd vapor to left and right.

sentences.zh: 章宗明昌三年十二月丙辰，北方微有赤氣。

translations.literal: Zhangzong, Mingchang third year, twelfth month, on bingchen: the north had a slight red vapor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangzong's third Mingchang year, on bingchen in the twelfth month, the north showed a slight red vapor.

sentences.zh: 四年九月癸未，日上有抱氣二，戴氣一，俱相連。

translations.literal: Fourth year, ninth month, on guiwei: on the sun were two embracing vapors and one cap vapor, all linked together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on guiwei in the ninth month, the sun bore two embracing vapors and one cap vapor, all joined.

sentences.zh: 左右有珥，其色鮮明。

translations.literal: Left and right had parhelia; their color was bright and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Parhelia appeared to left and right, bright and distinct.

sentences.zh: 六年三月丙戌朔，日食。

translations.literal: Sixth year, third month, on bingxu new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on bingxu new moon in the third month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 承安三年正月己亥朔，日食，陰雲不見。

translations.literal: Cheng'an third year, first month, on jihai new moon: solar eclipse; overcast clouds—it was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Cheng'an year, on jihai new moon in the first month, there was a solar eclipse, but clouds hid it.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月癸丑，日食。

translations.literal: Fifth year, eleventh month, on guichou: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on guichou in the eleventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《宋史》作六月乙酉朔。

translations.literal: The Song History gives sixth month, on yiyou new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Song History records it as yiyou new moon in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年五月甲辰朔，日食。

translations.literal: Taihe second year, fifth month, on jiachen new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Taihe year, on jiachen new moon in the fifth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 三年十月戊戌，日將沒，色赤如赭。

translations.literal: Third year, tenth month, on wuxu: as the sun was about to set, its color was red like ochre.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on wuxu in the tenth month, the setting sun turned red as ochre.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，申酉間，天色赤，夜將旦複然。

translations.literal: On jiachen, between shen and you hours, the sky was red; as night was about to dawn it happened again.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, between shen and you, the sky turned red; near dawn it did so again.

sentences.zh: 四年三月丁卯，日昏無光。

translations.literal: Fourth year, third month, on dingmao: the sun was dim and without light.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on dingmao in the third month, the sun was dim and lightless.

sentences.zh: 五年九月戊子戌時，西北方黑雲間有赤氣如火，次及西南、正南、東南方皆赤，中有白氣貫徹，乍隱乍見。

translations.literal: Fifth year, ninth month, on wuzi at the xu watch: among black clouds in the northwest was red vapor like fire; next the southwest, due south, and southeast all turned red, with white vapor piercing through, now hidden, now seen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on wuzi in the ninth month at the xu watch, red fire-like vapor appeared in northwestern black clouds, then spread to the southwest, south, and southeast, pierced by white vapor that flickered in and out.

sentences.zh: 既而為雨，隨作風。

translations.literal: Then it became rain, and wind followed.
translations.idiomatic: Rain followed, then wind.

sentences.zh: 至二更初，黑雲間赤氣複起于西北方，及正西、正東、東北，往來遊曳，內有白氣數道，時複出沒。

translations.literal: By the start of the second watch, red vapor among black clouds rose again in the northwest, and in the due west, due east, and northeast, drifting back and forth; within were several white vapors that now appeared, now vanished.
translations.idiomatic: By the start of the second watch red vapor rose again from black clouds in the northwest and drifted across the west, east, and northeast, with several white vapors appearing and vanishing within.

sentences.zh: 其赤氣又滿中天，約四更皆散。

translations.literal: The red vapor again filled the zenith; about the fourth watch all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The red vapor again filled the sky and dispersed around the fourth watch.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，北京申，龍山縣西見有雲結成車牛行帳之狀，或如前後摧損之勢，晡時乃散。

translations.literal: Sixth year, first month, at the Northern Capital in the shen hour: west of Longshan county clouds formed the shapes of ox-carts and marching pavilions, some as if thrust forward or broken from before and behind; at the bu hour they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year's first month, at the Northern Capital in the shen hour, west of Longshan county clouds shaped like ox-carts and field pavilions, some as if pushed or shattered fore and aft; by the bu hour they broke up.

sentences.zh: 二月壬子朔，日食。

translations.literal: Second month, on renzi new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 七月癸巳，申刻，日有上背氣一，內赤外青，須臾散。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on guisi at the shen watch: the sun had one upper counter-glow, red within and green without; in a moment it dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on guisi at the shen watch, the sun showed one upper counter-glow, red within and green without, and soon faded.

sentences.zh: 九月乙酉，夜將曙，北方有赤白氣數道，曆王良下，徐行至北斗開陽、搖光之東而散。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on yiyou, as night was about to brighten: in the north were several red and white vapors; they passed below Wangliang and slowly moved east of the Dipper's Kaiyang and Yaoguang, then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the ninth month, near dawn, several red and white vapors in the north passed below Wangliang and drifted east of Kaiyang and Yaoguang before dispersing.

sentences.zh: 八年四月癸卯，巳刻，日暈二重，風黃外赤，移時而散。

translations.literal: Eighth year, fourth month, on guimao at the si watch: the sun had a double halo, feng-yellow within and red without; after a while it dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on guimao in the fourth month at the si watch, the sun had a double halo, yellow within and red without, and soon faded.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐元年十月丙午，夜有白氣三，沖紫微而貫。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, first Zhenyou year, tenth month, on bingwu: at night were three white vapors that struck Ziwei and pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzong's first Zhenyou year, on bingwu in the tenth month, three white vapors at night struck Ziwei and ran through it.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙申，白氣東西竟天，移時散。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on bingshen: white vapor spanned east and west across heaven; after a while it dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingshen, white vapor stretched east and west across the sky, then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 二年九月壬戌朔，日食，大星皆見。

translations.literal: Second year, ninth month, on renxu new moon: solar eclipse; the great stars were all visible.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on renxu new moon in the ninth month, there was a solar eclipse and the bright stars were all visible.

sentences.zh: 三年正月壬戌，日有左右珥，上有冠氣，移刻散。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, on renxu: the sun had parhelia left and right and crown vapor above; after a watch-period it dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on renxu in the first month, the sun had parhelia to left and right and crown vapor above; after a watch-period it faded.

sentences.zh: 二月丁巳，日初出赤如血，將沒複然。

translations.literal: Second month, on dingsi: at the sun's first rising it was red like blood; as it was about to set it was the same again.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the second month the rising sun was blood-red, and the same at its setting.

sentences.zh: 六月戊申，夜有黑氣，廣如大路，自東南至於西北，其長竟天。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on wushen: at night was black vapor as broad as a great road, from southeast to northwest; its length spanned heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the sixth month, black vapor broad as a great road stretched from southeast to northwest across the sky.

sentences.zh: 四年二月甲申朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fourth year, second month, on jiashen new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on jiashen new moon in the second month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 閏七月壬午朔，日食。

translations.literal: Intercalary seventh month, on renwu new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month, on renwu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 興定元年七月丙子朔，日食。

translations.literal: Xingding first year, seventh month, on bingzi new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Xingding year, on bingzi new moon in the seventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 二年七月庚午朔，日食。

translations.literal: Second year, seventh month, on gengwu new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on gengwu new moon in the seventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 三年七月庚申，五色雲見。

translations.literal: Third year, seventh month, on gengshen: five-colored clouds appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on gengshen in the seventh month, five-colored clouds appeared.

sentences.zh: 十月乙丑，平涼府慶雲見，遣官驗實，以告太廟，詔國中。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on yichou: at Pingliang prefecture auspicious clouds appeared; officials were sent to verify, report to the Grand Temple, and proclaim throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the tenth month auspicious clouds appeared at Pingliang; officials verified the sight, reported to the Grand Temple, and an edict announced it empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，山東行省蒙古綱奏慶雲見，命圖以進。

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month: the Shandong Branch Secretariat's Menggu Gang memorialized that auspicious clouds had appeared; he was ordered to submit a painting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's first month Menggu Gang of the Shandong Branch Secretariat reported auspicious clouds and was ordered to present a painting.

sentences.zh: 四月丙子，日正午，有黃暈四匝，其色鮮明。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on bingzi: at noon the sun had a yellow halo on all four sides; its color was bright and clear.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the fourth month, at noon the sun showed a bright yellow halo on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 五月甲申朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jiashen new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiashen new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 六月戊寅，日將出，有氣如大道，經醜未，曆虛危，東西不見首尾，移時沒。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on wuyin: as the sun was about to rise, vapor like a great road passed through Chou and Wei, crossed Xu and Wei; east and west its ends were not seen; after a while it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the sixth month, as the sun was about to rise, vapor like a great road ran through Chou and Wei and crossed Xu and Wei, its ends unseen east and west; after a while it disappeared.

sentences.zh: 十二月己巳，北方有白氣，廣三尺餘，東西亙天。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on jisi, in the north there was white vapor more than three chi wide, stretching east and west across the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jisi, white vapor over three chi wide in the north stretched east to west across the sky.

sentences.zh: 元光元年十一月丁未，東北有赤雲如火。

translations.literal: First year of Yuanguang, eleventh month, on dingwei, in the northeast was red cloud like fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanguang, eleventh month, on dingwei, red clouds like fire appeared in the northeast.

sentences.zh: 二年五月辛未，日暈不匝而有背氣。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, on xinwei, the sun had a halo that did not complete the circuit and had a counter-glow.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, fifth month, on xinwei, the sun showed an incomplete halo with a counter-glow.

sentences.zh: 九月庚子朔，日食。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on gengzi new moon, solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the gengzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 哀宗正大二年正月甲申，有黃黑昆。

translations.literal: Aizong, second year of Zhengda, first month, on jiashen, there was yellow-black intermingling.
translations.idiomatic: In Aizong's second year of Zhengda, first month, on jiashen, yellow and black mingled in the sky.

sentences.zh: 三年月三月庚午，省前有氣微黃，自東北亙西南，其狀如虹，中有白物十餘，往來飛翔，又有光倏見如二星，移時方滅。

translations.literal: Third year, third month, on gengwu, before the provincial office was faint yellow vapor from the northeast spanning the southwest; its form was like a rainbow, with more than ten white things within flying to and fro; also light appeared suddenly like two stars and after a time was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, third month, on gengwu, faint yellow vapor ran from northeast to southwest before the provincial office like a rainbow; more than ten white objects flew within it, and light flashed like two stars before fading.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月乙未，日上有虹，背而向外者二，約長丈餘，兩旁俱有白虹貫之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eleventh month, on yiwei, on the sun was a rainbow; two turning outward from the back, about a zhang long; on both sides white rainbows pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, eleventh month, on yiwei, a rainbow lay on the sun with two arcs turning outward from the back, about a zhang long, and white rainbows pierced them on either side.

sentences.zh: 是年六月丙辰，有白氣經天。

translations.literal: That year, sixth month, on bingchen, white vapor crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: That year, sixth month, on bingchen, white vapor stretched across the sky.

sentences.zh: 或雲太白入井。

translations.literal: Some say Great White entered the Well.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Venus had entered the Well.

sentences.zh: 五年十二庚子朔，日食。

translations.literal: Fifth year, twelfth month, on gengzi new moon, solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, twelfth month, on the gengzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 八年三月庚戌酉正，日忽白而失色，乍明乍暗，左右有氣似日而無光，與日相淩，而日光四出搖盪至沒。

translations.literal: Eighth year, third month, on gengxu at the correct hour of you, the sun suddenly turned white and lost color, now bright now dim; on left and right was vapor like the sun but without light, encroaching on the sun, and sunlight shot out in four directions swaying until it set.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, third month, on gengxu at the you hour, the sun paled and flickered; vapor like a sun without light pressed it on either side, and its rays shook in four directions until it set.

sentences.zh: 月五星淩犯及星變

translations.literal: Lunar and Five Planets Encroachments and Star Changes
translations.idiomatic: Lunar and Five-Planet Encroachments and Changes among the Stars

sentences.zh: 太宗天會七年十月甲寅，天旗明，河鼓直。

translations.literal: Taizong, seventh year of Tianhui, tenth month, on jiayin, the Celestial Banner was bright and the River Drum upright.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's seventh year of Tianhui, tenth month, on jiayin, the Celestial Banner shone bright and the River Drum stood straight.

sentences.zh: 十年閏四月丙申，熒惑入氐。

translations.literal: Tenth year, intercalary fourth month, on bingchen, Sparkling Deluder entered Root.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, intercalary fourth month, on bingchen, Mars entered Root.

sentences.zh: 八月辛亥，彗星出於文昌。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on xinhai, a comet appeared from Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai, a comet appeared at Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月乙丑，月忽失行而南。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, fifth month, on yichou, the moon suddenly lost its path and went south.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, fifth month, on yichou, the moon suddenly left its course and moved south.

sentences.zh: 頃之複故。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward it returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward it resumed its proper course.

sentences.zh: 七月己巳昏，有大星隕于東南，如散火。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on jisi at dusk, a large star fell in the southeast like scattered fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jisi at dusk, a great star fell in the southeast like scattered fire.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙戌，月食昴。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on bingxu, lunar eclipse at Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, the moon was eclipsed at Hairy Head.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天會十三年十一月乙酉，月食，命有司用幣以救，著為命。

translations.literal: Xizong, thirteenth year of Tianhui, eleventh month, on yiyou, lunar eclipse; he ordered the offices to use silks to rescue it, and this was established as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: In Xizong's thirteenth year of Tianhui, eleventh month, on yiyou, there was a lunar eclipse; he ordered the offices to offer silks to avert it, and this was made a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月辛巳，太白晝見，凡四十餘日伏。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, first month, on xinsi, Great White was seen in daytime; in all more than forty days then it set.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, first month, on xinsi, Venus was seen by day for more than forty days before it set.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，熒惑入月。

translations.literal: On renchen, Sparkling Deluder entered the moon.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Mars entered the moon.

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉夜，中星搖。

translations.literal: Third month, on dingyou at night, the Central Star shook.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingyou at night, the Central Star trembled.

sentences.zh: 九月癸未，有星大如缶，起西南，流於正西。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on guiwei, there was a star as large as a jar, rising in the southwest and streaming to due west.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiwei, a star as large as a jar rose in the southwest and streamed due west.

sentences.zh: 十一月己巳，狼星搖。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on jisi, the Wolf Star shook.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jisi, the Wolf Star trembled.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月戊辰，歲星犯積屍氣。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, first month, on wuchen, the Year Star encroached on Accumulated Corpse Breath.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, first month, on wuchen, Jupiter encroached on Accumulated Corpse Breath.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年三月辛巳朔，歲星留逆在太微。

translations.literal: Second year of Tianjuan, third month, on xinsi new moon, the Year Star stayed retrograde in Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan, third month, on the xinsi new moon, Jupiter halted retrograde in Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 五月戊子，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on wuzi, Great White was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Venus was seen by day.

sentences.zh: 八月丁丑，太白晝見；

translations.literal: Eighth month, on dingchou, Great White was seen in daytime;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingchou, Venus was seen by day.

sentences.zh: 九月辛巳，犯軒轅左星；

translations.literal: Ninth month, on xinsi, it encroached on Yellow Thearch's left star;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinsi, it encroached on the left star of Yellow Thearch.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，犯左執法；

translations.literal: On yisi, it encroached on Left Law-Enforcer;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, it encroached on Left Law-Enforcer.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊寅，入氐。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on wuyin, it entered Root.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuyin, it entered Root.

sentences.zh: 三年七月壬戌，月犯畢。

translations.literal: Third year, seventh month, on renxu, the moon encroached on Net.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, seventh month, on renxu, the moon encroached on Net.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬午，月掩東井東轅南第一星。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on renwu, the moon covered Eastern Well's eastern axle southern first star.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renwu, the moon covered the first star on the southern axle of Eastern Well's eastern hub.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年二月甲戌，月犯掩畢大星。

translations.literal: First year of Huangtong, second month, on jiaxu, the moon encroached and covered Net's great star.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangtong, second month, on jiaxu, the moon encroached and covered Net's great star.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月己酉，月犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: Second year, eleventh month, on jiyou, the moon encroached Yellow Thearch's great star.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, eleventh month, on jiyou, the moon encroached Yellow Thearch's great star.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，月犯氐東北星。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the moon encroached Root's northeastern star.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the moon encroached Root's northeastern star.

sentences.zh: 三年正月己丑，熒惑逆犯軒轅次北一星。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, on jichou, Sparkling Deluder in retrograde encroached Yellow Thearch's second northern star.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, on jichou, Mars in retrograde encroached Yellow Thearch's second northern star.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，月犯畢大星。

translations.literal: Second month, on yichou, the moon encroached Net's great star.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yichou, the moon encroached Net's great star.

sentences.zh: 閏四月癸巳，月掩軒轅左角星。

translations.literal: Intercalary fourth month, on guisi, the moon covered Yellow Thearch's left horn star.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month, on guisi, the moon covered Yellow Thearch's left horn star.

sentences.zh: 八月丙申，老人星見。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on bingshen, the Old Man Star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingshen, Canopus appeared.

sentences.zh: 九月丁丑，月犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on dingchou, the moon encroached Yellow Thearch's great star.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingchou, the moon encroached Yellow Thearch's great star.

sentences.zh: 四年八月癸未，熒惑入輿鬼。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eighth month, on guiwei, Sparkling Deluder entered Carriage Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, eighth month, on guiwei, Mars entered Carriage Ghosts.

sentences.zh: 五年四月丙申，彗星見於西北，長丈餘，至五月壬戌始滅。

translations.literal: Fifth year, fourth month, on bingshen, a comet appeared in the northwest, one zhang long; until fifth month on renxu it was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, fourth month, on bingshen, a comet one zhang long appeared in the northwest and was gone by renxu in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 六月甲辰，熒惑犯左執法。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on jiachen, Sparkling Deluder encroached Left Law-Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Mars encroached Left Law-Enforcer.

sentences.zh: 六年九月戊寅，熒惑犯西垣上將。

translations.literal: Sixth year, ninth month, on wuyin, Sparkling Deluder encroached the Western Rampart's Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, ninth month, on wuyin, Mars encroached the Western Rampart's Senior General.

sentences.zh: 己丑，月犯軒轅第二星。

translations.literal: On jichou, the moon encroached Yellow Thearch's second star.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the moon encroached Yellow Thearch's second star.

sentences.zh: 七年正月辛未，彗星出東方，長丈餘，凡十五日滅。

translations.literal: Seventh year, first month, on xinwei, a comet appeared in the east, one zhang long; in all fifteen days it was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, first month, on xinwei, a comet one zhang long appeared in the east and was gone in fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，太白經天。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Great White crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Venus crossed the sky.

sentences.zh: 七月己巳，太白經天。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on jisi, Great White crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jisi, Venus crossed the sky.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，熒惑犯房第二星。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Mars encroached upon the second star of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Mars encroached upon the second star of Fang.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬戌，歲星逆犯井東扇第二星。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renxu, Jupiter in retrograde encroached upon the second star of the eastern fan of the Well.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renxu, retrograde Jupiter encroached upon the second star of the Well's eastern fan.

sentences.zh: 八年閏八月丙子，熒惑入太微垣。

translations.literal: Eighth year, intercalary eighth month, on bingzi, Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, intercalary eighth month, on bingzi, Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 十月甲申，太白晝見；

translations.literal: Tenth month, on jiashen, Venus appeared in daylight;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jiashen, Venus shone by day;

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，經天。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renchen, it crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renchen, it crossed the sky.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on bingyin, Venus appeared in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingyin, Venus shone by day.

sentences.zh: 九年二年癸亥，月掩軒轅第二星。

translations.literal: Ninth year, second month, on guihai, the moon occulted the second star of Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, second month, on guihai, the moon occulted the second star of Xuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 七月甲辰，太白、辰星、歲星合于張。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on jiachen, Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter conjoined at Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jiachen, Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter conjoined at Zhang.

sentences.zh: 丁未，熒惑犯南斗第四星。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Mars encroached upon the fourth star of the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Mars encroached upon the fourth star of the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 八月壬子，又曆南斗第三星。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on renzi, it again passed through the third star of the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi, it again traversed the third star of the Southern Dipper.

translations.literal: Tianxing, first year, seventh month, on yisi, Venus, Jupiter, Mars, and the moon all met at Chariot Shaft and Wings. Director of Astronomy Wu Kang spoke urgently of Heaven's warning; the emperor only sighed, and in the end did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing, seventh month, on yisi, Venus, Jupiter, Mars, and the moon all gathered at Chariot Shaft and Wings. Wu Kang of the Bureau of Astronomy pressed hard on the celestial omen; the emperor could only sigh and did not punish him after all.

sentences.zh: 八月甲戌，太白、歲星交。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiaxu, Venus and Jupiter crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, on jiaxu, Venus and Jupiter crossed paths.

sentences.zh: 閏九月己酉，彗星見東方，色白，長丈餘，彎曲如象牙，出角、軫南行，至十二日長二丈，十六日月燭不見，二十七日五更複出東南，約長四丈餘，至十月一日始滅，凡四十有八日。

translations.literal: Intercalary ninth month, on jiyou, a comet appeared in the east, white in color, more than a zhang long, curved like ivory; it issued south of Horn and Chariot Shaft, and by the twelfth day was two zhang long; on the sixteenth the moon's light drowned it from sight; on the twenty-seventh at the fifth watch it again emerged in the southeast, about four zhang long or more, and only on the first day of the tenth month was extinguished—in all forty-eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary ninth month, on jiyou, a white comet more than a zhang long, curved like ivory, appeared in the east and moved south from Horn and Chariot Shaft; by the twelfth day it stretched two zhang; on the sixteenth moonlight hid it; on the twenty-seventh at the fifth watch it reappeared in the southeast, some four zhang long or more, and did not vanish until the first day of the tenth month—forty-eight days in all.

sentences.zh: 司天奏其咎在北，哀宗曰：「我亦北人，今日之事，我當滅也，何乃不先不後，適丁此乎！」

translations.literal: The Director of Astronomy reported that the blame lay in the north. Aizong said: "I too am a northerner. Given today's affairs, it is I who must perish—why did it come neither early nor late, but strike just now?"
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Astronomy said the omen pointed north. Aizong said, "I too am a man of the north. With things as they stand today, it is I who must fall—why neither sooner nor later, but timed to land on me now?"
